thread:
elaine: FYI escalation from a big customer. They hit repeated parse failures in JSON mode when sending nested order batches. Attaching the minimal repro and logs they gave.

matt: Can you paste the exact request and the model output?

elaine: Request body (trimmed):
```json
{
  "json_mode": "json_array",
  "orders": [
    {
      "order_id": "o_123",
      "items": [
        {"sku": "A1", "qty": 1},
        {"sku": "B2", "qty": 2}
      ]
    },
    {
      "items": [
        {"sku": "C3", "qty": 1}  
      ],
      "temp_ref": "t-999"  
    }
  ]
}
```

elaine: Model response (streamed, truncated):
```
[
  {
    \"order_id\": \"o_123\",\n    \"items\": [{\"sku\":\"A1\",\"qty\":1},{\"sku\":\"B2\",\"qty\":2}]
  },
  {
    \"sku\": \"C3\",\n    \"qty\": 1,\n    \"temp_ref\": \"t-999\"
  }
]
```

anna: Ugh — second array element flattened into top-level item; customer schema expects `order_id` required for each order object, so downstream validator fails. They see parse errors when validating against OpenAPI.

matt: Do we have a streaming boundary bug where the model emits a partial object and then resumes with different shape? Might be tokenization-induced field shifting. Any streaming logs?

elaine: Here's the error from the customer's validator: `ValidationError: Missing required property: order_id at index 1` and our gateway log shows: `parse_error: json_parse_failed at byte=482 token=unexpected_value`.

support-bot: Ticket created: SUP-4228. Assigned to eng-ml. ETA for triage: 3 business hours.

matt: Repro steps I ran locally against our hosted endpoint using json_array mode: 1) send request above 2) enable streaming 3) collect chunks 4) naive concat -> sometimes returns flattened second object. Intermittent ~20% on my run.

matt: Sample model output chunk sequence (chunk boundaries marked):
```
chunk1: "[\n  {\n    \"order_id\": \"o_123\",\n    \"items\": [\n      {\"sku\":\"A1\",\"qty\":1},\n"
chunk2: "{\"sku\":\"B2\",\"qty\":2}]\n  },\n"
chunk3: "  {\n    \"items\": [\n      {\"sku\":\"C3\",\"qty\":1}\n    ],\n"
chunk4: "    \"temp_ref\": \"t-999\"\n  }\n]\n"
```

matt: When concatenated these should parse. But if a consumer applies a streaming JSON frame parser that expects object-per-chunk, a mid-object boundary with extra key ordering can cause theirs to treat an inner item as top-level. So it's a client deserializer assumption + schema drift combo.

anna: Customer says they do NOT use streaming-aware parser; they just do line-by-line assembly. Their fast-path code uses a regex to split on `\n\n` and then json.loads(first_line). So it's brittle.

elaine: They flagged this to support because their validation pipeline is strict and fails on missing required fields — billing impact from dropped orders reported. They want a quick mitigation.

matt: Short-term mitigation suggestions we gave: 1) turn off streaming (get full body) 2) ask customer to use a tolerant joiner that accumulates until balanced brackets (track open/close braces) 3) pin model to non-streaming variant or increase max_tokens window to reduce chunking.

anna: Long-term: we should harden our streaming framing by emitting explicit "frame" separators or ensure chunks don't split tokens in a way that encourages consumers to mis-interpret object boundaries. Also update docs with recommended robust consumer patterns (bracket counting, JSON streaming libs).

sre-oncall: Also flagging eng-runtime: if the runtime chooses different kernel packing across requests, chunk boundary characteristics might change. Could be correlated with batching and KV cache alignment.

matt: For this specific case there's also an issue of extra keys (`temp_ref`) in nested objects — schema drift. If downstream validators are strict, small extra fields shouldn't cause flattening but combined with their brittle line-splitting it did. We should add a note in support reply to ask for their exact parser code and offer a diff for a safe join function.

elaine: Customer replied they can turn off streaming for now. They've requested a postmortem and a recommended fix they can apply to their validator to avoid billing breaks.

anna: I'll draft the postmortem and the code snippet to recommend. Example safe join pseudo: `accum = ''; for chunk in stream: accum += chunk; if bracket_balance(accum) == 0: objs.append(json.loads(accum)); accum = ''`

matt: Adding engineering owners: @eng-ml for model tokenization/emit behavior, @eng-runtime for framing, @devex for docs update.

support-bot: Note: escalated to eng-ml and eng-runtime. Priority: P2.

elaine: Closing loop: customer satisfied with workaround but requests timeline for a runtime fix. We'll keep them updated in SUP-4228.

matt: Action items: eng-ml to reproduce under varied batching, eng-runtime to evaluate emitting stronger frame boundaries or metadata, devex to publish streaming parser guidance.

anna: Thanks, closing for now. :white_check_mark:
